name: The men of Succoth and Penuel
charge: Refusing bread to the army of the Lord, faint yet pursuing, and upbraiding them with it
summary: Gideon and the three hundred crossed the Jordan exhausted but still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna the kings of Midian, and asked the men of Succoth for bread. The princes of Succoth asked whether he already had the two kings in hand, that they should feed his army, and the men of Penuel answered the same way, both cities playing neutral for fear the kings might come back on them. He told each of them what he would do when the Lord had given the kings into his hand, and he came back with the kings in hand. He taught the elders of Succoth with thorns and briers and tore down the tower of Penuel.
offenseFull: Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed with his three hundred men, exhausted but still pursuing, and asked the men of Succoth for bread for the people with him, because they were worn out while he chased Zebah and Zalmunna the kings of Midian. The princes of Succoth sneered, asking whether he already had the two kings in hand, that they should feed his army; and when he went on to Penuel and asked the same, the men of Penuel gave the same answer (Judges 8:4-6). Both cities were playing neutral ground out of fear that the kings of Midian might come against them for helping. Two cities of Israel watched the army of the Lord come through faint and weary from the deliverance of the whole nation, and made their help depend on a victory that was not finished yet.

Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men, all that remained of the eastern armies, for a hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen (Judges 8:4-12). Three hundred men against those numbers on an empty stomach, and you know God was with them. Those two kings are the princes named in Asaph’s prayer, which asks that God’s enemies be made like Oreb and Zeeb and their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna (Psalms 83:11).
judgmentFull: Gideon promised Succoth that when the Lord had given Zebah and Zalmunna into his hand he would thresh their flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness, and promised Penuel that when he came back in peace he would tear down their tower (Judges 8:7-9). He came around by the road of the tent dwellers, struck the camp while it felt safe, chased down the two kings, captured them, and routed the whole army. On the way back he caught a young man of Succoth who gave him the names of the princes and elders of the city, and he came back with the kings in hand and showed the men of Succoth the very prisoners they had mocked him about. He took the elders of the city and taught the men of Succoth with the thorns and briers of the wilderness (Judges 8:13-16). He taught them a lesson: when the army of the Lord comes through faint and weary and asks for bread, you do not turn it away. And he tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna what the men they had killed at Tabor looked like, and they said each one looked like a king’s son, just like him; they were his own brothers, his

mother’s sons, and he told the kings that if they had spared them he would have spared the kings (Judges 8:13-21). He told Jether his firstborn to get up and kill them, but the boy did not draw his sword, because he was afraid, being still young. We have all had that moment of getting the nudge from our father and being nervous; the son was young, and that is understandable, but look at what Gideon was doing, taking his son to the war and teaching him the way he must walk, which is exactly what we have to do with our young men, training a boy early in the path he is to keep (Proverbs 22:6). Zebah and Zalmunna told Gideon to do it himself, since a man’s strength matches the man; they wanted to die quickly at the hand of a warrior rather than suffer under the sword of a boy. So Gideon killed them and took the ornaments from their camels’ necks.

text.text: And Gideon came to Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint, yet pursuing them.
And he said unto the men of Succoth, Give, I pray you, loaves of bread unto the people that follow me; for they be faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian.
And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?
And Gideon came to Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint, yet pursuing them.
And he said unto the men of Succoth, Give, I pray you, loaves of bread unto the people that follow me; for they be faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian.
And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?
And Gideon said, Therefore when the Lord hath delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into mine hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.
And he went up thence to Penuel, and spake unto them likewise: and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered him.
And he spake also unto the men of Penuel, saying, When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.

Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their hosts with them, about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of all the hosts of the children of the east: for there fell an hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword.
And Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and smote the host: for the host was secure.
And when Zebah and Zalmunna fled, he pursued after them, and took the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and discomfited all the host.
Make their nobles like Oreb, and like Zeeb: yea, all their princes as Zebah, and as Zalmunna:
And Gideon said, Therefore when the Lord hath delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into mine hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.
And he went up thence to Penuel, and spake unto them likewise: and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered him.
And he spake also unto the men of Penuel, saying, When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.
And Gideon the son of Joash returned from battle before the sun was up,
And caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and enquired of him: and he described unto him the princes of Succoth, and the elders thereof, even threescore and seventeen men.

And he came unto the men of Succoth, and said, Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, with whom ye did upbraid me, saying, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thy men that are weary?
And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.
And Gideon the son of Joash returned from battle before the sun was up,
And caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and enquired of him: and he described unto him the princes of Succoth, and the elders thereof, even threescore and seventeen men.

And he came unto the men of Succoth, and said, Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, with whom ye did upbraid me, saying, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thy men that are weary?
And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.
And he beat down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city.
Then said he unto Zebah and Zalmunna, What manner of men were they whom ye slew at Tabor? And they answered, As thou art, so were they; each one resembled the children of a king.
And he said, They were my brethren, even the sons of my mother: as the Lord liveth, if ye had saved them alive, I would not slay you.
And he said unto Jether his firstborn, Up, and slay them. But the youth drew not his sword: for he feared, because he was yet a youth.

Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon arose, and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels’ necks.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
